title: House Robber II
prompt:
Same as House Robber, but the houses are arranged in a **circle** — the first and last are adjacent, so you can't rob both. Return the max loot.

**Example**: `[2,3,2]` → `3` (can't take both 2s).

Run the linear House Robber twice: once excluding the last house, once excluding the first; take the better.
hints: The circular constraint means house 0 and house n-1 can't both be robbed.
So the answer is max( rob houses [0 .. n-2], rob houses [1 .. n-1] ).
Handle a single house separately (no range to split).

solution.explanation: The circle only adds one coupling: first and last are neighbors. Excluding one end at a time breaks the circle into a line, reducing the problem to two runs of the linear O(n) House Robber. The better of the two respects the adjacency.
